name: chgrp
summary: Changes the group that owns files.
description: Gives files a new group, without touching the owner. A user can give one of their files to a group they belong to; beyond that, sudo is needed. chown :group file does the same thing.

options.description: Applies the change to directories and everything in them.
Prints a message for each file processed.
Prints only the files actually changed.

example.output: changed group of 'report.pdf' from esprit to team

options.description: Changes the symbolic link itself rather than its target.
Copies the group of another file.

arguments.name: GROUP
arguments.description: Name (or number) of the new group.

examples.explanation: The file now belongs to the developers group.
Gives the whole site to the web server’s group.
Changes the group and confirms it.
examples.output: changed group of 'report.pdf' from esprit to team
